target.title: fix(session-memory): use shortenHomePath for safe home-path display in logs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`saveSessionMemoryNow` in `src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.ts` uses `memoryFilePath.replace(os.homedir(), "~")` at two call sites to shorten home paths in log output. `String.replace()` is unbounded and corrupts sibling paths that happen to share the home prefix as a substring.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace with the existing `shortenHomePath()` utility from `src/utils.ts`, which checks `startsWith("${home}/")` boundaries. This is a one-line swap at each call site and the utility is already available in the import graph.

## User Impact

Log messages from the session-memory hook show corrupted paths when the user has a sibling directory sharing the home prefix (e.g., `/home/user` vs `/home/user2`).

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof — reproduced via node:**
```
Input:  "/home/user2/.openclaw/state/memory/test.md" (home=/home/user)
OLD:    "~2/.openclaw/state/memory/test.md"  <- corrupted
NEW:    "/home/user2/.openclaw/state/memory/test.md"  <- preserved
```

**Validation:**
- tsgo typecheck: passed
- `pnpm test src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.test.ts`: 29 tests passed
